Training details
Limitations
Employment Status excluded: it is 100% derived from Attrition (a direct label leak), so it's never used as a model input.

Salary excluded from the model: ~88% of Salary values in the source file are zero or negative and were treated as missing — too sparse to use reliably as a predictor (still shown in KPIs from the ~657 valid records).

Missing numeric inputs are imputed with the training-set median; missing categories become an "Unknown" bucket. This is a linear model trained entirely in the browser — treat outputs as directional signal, not a certified HR decision tool.

About this dashboard

Methodology, data quality notes and how this was built.

What this is

A self-contained HR analytics dashboard and attrition-risk model built from a single uploaded HR dataset. Everything — data cleaning, charting, the prediction model and its evaluation — runs client-side in this one HTML file. There is no server, no database and no build step.

Dataset

Cleaning rules applied

  • Fully blank rows and rows missing an Employee ID were dropped, and exact duplicate rows were removed.
  • Category labels were normalized for casing and stray whitespace (e.g. "FINANCE" / "finance " → "Finance"), and a known city misspelling was merged ("Banglore" → "Bengaluru").
  • Out-of-range values were treated as missing rather than used as-is: Age outside 16–85, Performance Rating outside 1–5, negative Training Hours, and Salary ≤ 0.

Prediction model

Binary logistic regression trained with batch gradient descent directly in JavaScript. Numeric features are standardized (z-scored) using training-set statistics; categorical features are one-hot encoded. The model is retrained automatically whenever a new file is uploaded.

Deploying this file

Upload index.html to a GitHub repository, then enable it under Settings → Pages. No npm install, no Python, no backend — it's a static file.
